snapshot.title: SSC Reasoning: Non-Verbal Reasoning
snapshot.exam_hook: ⚡ SSC Reasoning Hook: Mirror: L/R flip. Water: Up/Down flip. Unfold: Mirror across crease. Scan carefully. Symmetry is key.

quick_notes.title: Mirror Image
quick_notes.detail: Left becomes Right, Right becomes Left. (Horizontal flip). Vertical orientation remains same.
quick_notes.explanation: A mirror image is what you see when you look into a flat mirror, like the one in your bathroom. In a mirror image, the left side of an object appears on the right side of the reflection, and the right side appears on the left; this is called a horizontal flip. For example, if you raise your right hand, the person in the mirror appears to raise their left hand. However, the top and bottom of the object stay in the same place, meaning the vertical orientation does not change. So, a mirror image reverses left and right but keeps up and down exactly the same.

quick_notes.title: Water Image
quick_notes.detail: Top becomes Bottom, Bottom becomes Top. (Vertical flip). Horizontal orientation remains same.
quick_notes.explanation: A water image is what you see when you look at an object reflected in water, like a building reflected in a lake. In a water image, the top of the object becomes the bottom, and the bottom becomes the top; this is called a vertical flip. The horizontal orientation does not change, meaning the left side stays on the left and the right side stays on the right, so the object is not flipped sideways. For example, if a letter looks like a capital T, its water image will look the same because flipping it vertically does not change its shape, but a capital P will look like a capital d when flipped.

quick_notes.title: Paper Folding & Cutting
quick_notes.detail: The fold acts as a mirror line. Unfolding mirrors the pattern across the crease.
quick_notes.explanation: When you fold a piece of paper, the fold line itself acts like a mirror: it reflects whatever is on one side to the other side. This means that any shape you cut along the folded edge will appear on both sides when you open the paper back up. For example, if you fold the paper in half, then cut a small triangle along the folded edge, when you unfold the paper, you will see two identical triangles facing each other across the crease. The crease line is the mirror, and the cut pattern is mirrored exactly on the other side. So the final shape after folding and cutting is always symmetrical—one half is the mirror image of the other half.

quick_notes.title: Embedded Figures
quick_notes.detail: Finding a small pattern hidden within a larger, complex figure. Requires careful scanning.
quick_notes.explanation: Embedded Figures is a topic in reasoning where you look for a simple shape that is hidden inside a more complicated drawing. The simple shape is called the "figure," and the complicated drawing is called the "embedded figure." To solve this, you must carefully scan the larger picture with your eyes to find the exact outline of the small shape, which might be turned, stretched, or mixed with other lines. For example, if you are given a small triangle, you need to find where that same triangle appears as part of a bigger design, like a star or a house. This skill helps you practice paying close attention to detail and spotting patterns that are not obvious at first glance.

quick_notes.title: Completion of Figures
quick_notes.detail: Predicting the missing 1/4th of a pattern based on symmetry (horizontal/vertical).
quick_notes.explanation: In this lesson, we learn how to complete a figure that has part of its pattern missing. A figure is a shape or drawing, and a pattern is a design that repeats or is mirrored. The missing part is typically one-quarter (1/4) of the whole figure. To find that missing quarter, we use symmetry, which means one side is a mirror image of the other. Horizontal symmetry means the top half mirrors the bottom half, and vertical symmetry means the left half mirrors the right half. By looking at the three-quarters you already have, you can predict what the missing quarter should look like based on that mirror rule.
